questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y+z=-1 \\ x-y+3z=2 \\ -2x+y-z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, and the inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -8 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

the solution of the system of equations is 

$x=$
{{field-1}}, 
$\,y=$
{{field-2}}, 
$\,z=$
{{field-3}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -8 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 0 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is 

$$
x=-1,\,y=0,\,z=1.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+z=1 \\ 3x+2y-z=1 \\ x-4y+3z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ -10 & 2 & 4 \\ -14 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ -10 & 2 & 4 \\ -14 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=1,y=-2,z=-2.$

Finally, $x+y+z=1+(-2)+(-2)=-3.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=2 \\ x-2y-5z=-1 \\ 2x-3y+2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-19 & -7 & 11 \\ -12 & -4 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 2 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-19 & -7 & 11 \\ -12 & -4 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=5,y=3,z=0.$

Finally, $x+y+z=5+3+0=8.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z=0 \\ x+3y+z=-1 \\ 2x-3y-z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $\frac{yz}{x}?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & 0 \\ -9 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & -3 & 0 \\ -9 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=-1,y=-1,z=3.$

Finally, $\frac{yz}{x}=\frac{(-1)\cdot 3}{-1}=3.$

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}].

questions.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 \\ 7 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y+z=1 \\ 2x-2z=2+2y \\ 2y+4z=2x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Find  $x+y+z.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system in the correct order:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y+z=1 \\ 2x-2y-2z=2 \\ -2x+2y+4z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =0|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-(8-4)+(4-4) \\  & =-4+0 \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -4 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{-4}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x+y+z=2+1+0=3.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}4x-2y+3z=0 \\ 8x-3y+5z=9 \\ 7x-2y+4z=-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 \\ 7 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 9 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 \\ 7 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =4|\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}8 & 5 \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(-12+10)+2(32-35)+3(-16+21) \\  & =-8-6+15 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}8 & 5 \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 8 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 8 & -3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 5 \\ -2 & -5 & 6 \\ -1 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & -5 & -6 \\ -1 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 9 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}19 \\ -49 \\ -58\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=19,y=-49,z=-58.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2y+3z=-1-x \\ 4y=-5z \\ x+6z-3=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+2y+3z=-1 \\ 4y+5z=0 \\ x+6z=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(24)-2(-5)+3(0-4) \\  & =24+10-12 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}24 & -5 & -4 \\ 12 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}24 & 5 & -4 \\ -12 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}-30 \\ -20 \\ 16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{15}{11} \\ -\frac{10}{11} \\ \frac{8}{11}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=-\frac{15}{11},y=-\frac{10}{11},z=\frac{8}{11}.$

Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+z=4x+y+2 \\ x+y=2z+2 \\ y=x-y+z+1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution $x=[x,y,z]^{T}$ of the system by computing the inverse of the coefficient matrix.

|  |  | {{field-1}} |  |

questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system in the correct order:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x-y+z=2 \\ x+y-2z=2 \\ -x+2y-z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(-1+4)+(-1-2)+(2+1) \\  & =-9-3+3 \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -7 \\ 1 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 1 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -5 \\ 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -5 \\ 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -5 \\ 3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 9 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y+z+x=2 \\ -3z+y=3 \\ 2x+y=4-4z\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+y+z=2 \\ y-3z=3 \\ 2x+y+4z=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4+3)-(0+6)+(0-2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 6 & -2 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & -2 \\ -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & 3 & 1\text{ }\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -6 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=11,y=-6,z=-3.$

questions.problem: Consider a matrix equation $A\,x={B}^{-1}\,d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\times 2$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${A}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $A\,x={B}^{-1}\,d$ by ${A}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$

$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Given the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y-2z=-2 \\ -3y+z=-2 \\ 3x-7y+3z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}.$ Given that $\mathbf x = \langle x,y,z\rangle$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14053808/assets/add80202102548e61880979bc0379e0bc65f9ef7fa37173f9035410661e2b75e.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & -7 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by $\mathbf{x}= A^{-1}\mathbf{b}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=3, y=0, z=-2.$

Finally, $x+y+z=3+0+(-2)=1.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations By Calculating the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3y+x+z=0 \\ z+4y-5=2 \\ 1+2x-y=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are in the correct order and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+3y+z=0 \\ 0x+4y+z=7 \\ 2x-y+0z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14053808/assets/97d3c148b792d9db50bc81b8c12f1574f284746cb37b12d99a8881853bf5ea13.png)

Now, the solution to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by $\mathbf{x}= A^{-1}\mathbf{b}.$ So, we compute $A^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1*: Find the determinant of $A.$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(1)-3(-2)+(-8) \\  & =1+6-8 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2*: Compute the matrix of minors.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & -7 \\ -1 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3*:  Find the matrix of cofactors.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14053808/assets/e93ae11a2b2d1538c4ad97bba6d92e8e17fe14c8778898365ffeda9c5d1bacee.png)

*Step 4*: Transpose the matrix of cofactors.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14053808/assets/c2492650916d7a880ea52322edb41b8127b4c31bcff0620cec3cf4e37fa7928f.png)

*Step 5*: Apply the inverse matrix formula.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14053808/assets/dd70742ae3c6613f78305edc718b10568269b49be611643059a1e6121828f404.png)

Finally, we can calculate the solution as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10 \\ -33\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=3,$ $y=10,$ $z=-33.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse $B^{−1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\,\mathbf{d}$ by $B^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{10}\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$
